title: Terraform Introduces tfpolicy, an HCL-based Policy-as-Code Framework
gist: HashiCorp has put tfpolicy, an HCL-based policy-as-code framework, into public beta inside HCP Terraform, letting platform teams write governance rules in the same language as their infrastructure and evaluate them before and after deployment. Sentinel remains supported but tfpolicy is now the preferred framework, with an AI agent to convert existing Sentinel policies, and full enforcement is deliberately gated to the managed HCP Terraform product.

insights.claim: HashiCorp has released tfpolicy, an HCL-based policy-as-code framework for Terraform, in public beta within HCP Terraform.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: A beta-stage governance layer inside the incumbent IaC tool is the first move in displacing third-party policy engines.

insights.claim: Writing policies in HCL, the same language used to define Terraform infrastructure, removes the need for platform teams to switch tools and languages between authoring infrastructure and governing it.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Language consolidation is the adoption wedge: it lowers the switching cost from Sentinel and OPA to near zero for existing Terraform teams.
insights.quote: Terraform tfpolicy is deeply integrated into Terraform and uses HCL, the same language that enables the creation of Terraform infrastructure, thus reducing the need to switch tools and languages
insights.locator: Terraform tfpolicy is deeply integrated into Terraform

insights.claim: tfpolicy is positioned as a declarative framework that lets platform teams define and enforce policies in a familiar language while adding governance capabilities aimed at modern infrastructure systems.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Platform engineering teams are the buying centre being targeted, not security teams.
insights.quote: Terraform policy is a declarative, HCL-based policy as code framework that enables platform teams to define and enforce policies using a familiar language while introducing new governance capabilities designed for modern infrastructure systems.
insights.locator: Terraform policy is a declarative, HCL-based policy

insights.claim: Existing policy solutions such as HashiCorp Sentinel and Open Policy Agent operate as separate layers that validate infrastructure against policy rules, rather than being embedded in the provisioning workflow.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: The 'separate layer' framing is the argument HashiCorp will use to pull governance spend back in-house.
insights.locator: Existing solutions, such as HashiCorp Sentinel and Open Policy Agent

insights.claim: HashiCorp argues that separate-layer policy engines often fail to incorporate key external context such as relationships between resources, which change through the infrastructure lifecycle.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Resource-relationship awareness is the technical claim that would justify migrating away from OPA.
insights.locator: According to HashiCorp, these approaches often fails

insights.claim: Terraform will continue to support Sentinel, but HashiCorp is positioning tfpolicy as its preferred policy framework.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Sentinel is on a soft-deprecation path; investment in Sentinel tooling now carries migration risk.
insights.locator: Terraform will continue to support Sentinel

insights.claim: HashiCorp is shipping an AI agent that generates and tests tfpolicy configurations and converts existing Sentinel policies.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: An automated converter removes the main friction in a migration and accelerates Sentinel's retirement.
insights.locator: The company is also introducing an AI agent

insights.claim: Open Policy Agent's defensibility rests on being open-source, cloud-native, vendor-agnostic and supporting over 100 integrations, whereas Sentinel relies on a custom domain-specific language embedded natively in HCP Terraform.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: OPA's breadth beyond Terraform is what tfpolicy cannot easily attack; Sentinel's DSL is the vulnerable position.
insights.locator: HashiCorp Sentinel is an embedded policy-as-code framework

insights.claim: tfpolicy evaluates policies both before and after deployment, letting organizations detect violations that only become visible once resources have been provisioned.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Post-apply evaluation closes the drift gap that plan-time-only policy engines structurally cannot cover.
insights.quote: Teams can enforce requirements based on actual infrastructure state — not just planned changes — all within the familiar workflows and practices Terraform practitioners already use every day.
insights.locator: This deep integration brings governance closer to the infrastructure lifecycle

insights.claim: tfpolicy can evaluate policies based on relationships between resources and use data source lookups to pull external context into enforcement workflows.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Relationship- and lookup-aware rules are what let policy cover multi-cloud systems rather than individual resources.
insights.locator: tfpolicy also introduces several new capabilities

insights.claim: tfpolicy addresses supply-chain risk by controlling provider and module downloads so organizations can establish approved dependency controls and block unapproved providers or modules.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: IaC dependency control is an underserved attack surface; this is the feature most likely to force enterprise adoption.
insights.quote: establish approved dependency controls, and prevent accidental use of unapproved providers or modules
insights.locator: Additionally, it also addresses supply-chain risks

insights.claim: tfpolicy delivers its full capabilities only inside HCP Terraform, while the standalone CLI is limited mainly to policy validation and local testing without the same integration, automation or enforcement.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: The governance feature is a paid-platform pull: full enforcement requires buying HCP Terraform, which is the monetization mechanism to watch.
insights.quote: In contrast, the standalone CLI is more limited in scope, primarily supporting policy validation and local testing.
insights.locator: As a final note, tfpolicy delivers its full capabilities only within HCP Terraform

insights.claim: Policy enforcement in HCP Terraform spans planning, deployment and post-deployment evaluation as an end-to-end workflow, which is the integration the open CLI does not replicate.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: End-to-end lifecycle coverage is the lock-in argument against OpenTofu-style open alternatives.
insights.locator: where it can be tightly integrated into end-to-end infrastructure workflows
